I've pondered a time or two about setting about writing a post-*Die Another Day* story, where the aftermath of Bond's 14-month North Korean prison experience really gets to be explored. Ideas like Bond being saddled with BS missions due to lingering questions of his loyalty and mental stability, but passing every test thrown at him (even if a few are by the skin of his teeth, because various officials being extremely skeptical of anyone surviving what Bond did intact mentally or physically....Bond actually having thoughts of taking retirement but knowing he's aware of too many dirty secrets to be left alone for long and having zero backup or assistance once he's gone from MI-6...Moneypenny asking Bond to not carry out a mission or intentionally fail it because she knows his target and refuses to believe they've gone rogue/are dirty (allowing for a big scene between Bond and Moneypenny where he starts naming names like Trevelyan and Miranda Frost to emphasis that their business breeds traitors and Moneypenny fights back with how Bond's getting tarred with the same brush when he's proving the Powers That Be wrong).... That or working off of Max Landis' "Bond vs. Bond(s)" concept of Craig's Bond facing off against Dalton and Brosnan, who are prior 007s who have gone rogue...give the baddie Bonds justifiable reasons for their actions but not excuse them, weave a functional sense of continuity of the first 20 Bond films, force Craig's Bond to look at what the job could lead to if death while defending Queen & country doesn't find him...
